text_by_object_id.p1_i8: Egypt’s Red Sea water mile, inside inDrive
text_by_object_id.p1_i9: Focus on five short routes around Hurghada and Sharm El Sheikh. Keep Cairo as distribution context, not a marine route claim.
text_by_object_id.narr2_positioning: A Red Sea route proposal connected to the complete trip
text_by_object_id.narr2_thesis: inDrive can connect road journeys to short resort, island and reef crossings.
text_by_object_id.narr2_deal: Validate route demand, fares, terminals and operators before selecting a launch route.
text_by_object_id.narr2_w1_b: Five short routes around Hurghada and Sharm El Sheikh define the country proposal.
text_by_object_id.narr2_w2_b: Airport, hotel and excursion journeys fragment when the final leg moves onto the water.
text_by_object_id.narr2_w3_b: A booked electric connection can link road transport with island, reef and resort destinations.
text_by_object_id.narr2_w4_b: Route-level passenger demand, fares, terminal access and local operating partners.
text_by_object_id.g3f139a0b6ec_0_3: Three foundations for practical water transportation
text_by_object_id.g3f139a0b6ec_0_7:
Hydrofoiling lowers energy use at speed.
A uniform electric fleet simplifies operations.
text_by_object_id.g3f139a0b6ec_0_8:
Quiet electric propulsion.
A stable ride above the chop.
text_by_object_id.g3f139a0b6ec_0_9:
Book beside the car.
Connect waterfronts, islands and resorts.
text_by_object_id.g3eec5122801_0_4: Five short routes around two Red Sea cities
text_by_object_id.g3eec5122801_0_14: Hurghada and Sharm El Sheikh are the marine focus. Cairo remains relevant for trip distribution and airport connections only.
text_by_object_id.g3eec5122801_0_19: Cairo marine routes in this proposal
text_by_object_id.g3eec5122801_0_111: A short excursion connection from the city marina to Orange Bay and Mahmya.
text_by_object_id.g3eec5122801_0_114:
▸  Hurghada Marina → Giftun Island
      ~6.6 nm · island and beach-club access
text_by_object_id.didi_cancun_subtitle: Sahl Hasheesh and Soma Bay create separate route and operating questions.
text_by_object_id.didi_cancun_routes:
▸  Hurghada Marina → Sahl Hasheesh Marina
      ~9.5 nm · short resort-coast connection

▸  Hurghada Marina → Soma Bay Marina
      ~24.2 nm · longer resort corridor
text_by_object_id.didi_playa_subtitle: A short marine connection from Old Market Harbour toward the national-park reef area.
text_by_object_id.didi_playa_routes:
▸  Sharm Marina → Ras Mohammed
      ~11.7 nm · reef and excursion access
text_by_object_id.didi_vallarta_subtitle: A short connection between two named local waterfront facilities.
text_by_object_id.didi_vallarta_routes:
▸  Sharm Marina → Sharks Bay Marina
      ~5.4 nm · local marina-to-marina connection
text_by_object_id.didi_cabos_title: Cairo is not a marine route in this proposal
text_by_object_id.didi_cabos_subtitle: Its role is trip discovery, airport and intercity distribution toward the Red Sea.
text_by_object_id.didi_cabos_routes:
▸  Cairo demand → Red Sea booking
      screen trip origination and customer acquisition

▸  Airport and road leg → Hurghada or Sharm
      connect the surface journey before the water leg

▸  Marine proposal → Red Sea cities
      keep the operating case local
text_by_object_id.didi_nicoya_title: Prove each route before a launch decision
text_by_object_id.didi_nicoya_subtitle: The country proposal defines the routes and questions; the financial case follows route-level evidence.
text_by_object_id.didi_nicoya_routes:
▸  Demand → Named route
      annual one-way passengers

▸  Fare → Named route
      current comparable one-way price

▸  Operations → Named terminals
      access, permissions and local operator

▸  Service design → Named route
      schedule, weather and charging plan
text_by_object_id.g3eec5122801_0_565: Five routes are defined; route-level inputs come next
text_by_object_id.g3eec5122801_0_567: The current workbook shows the five Egypt routes separately and excludes them from financial totals until demand and fare evidence is available.
text_by_object_id.g3eec5122801_0_587: Source annual demand and route fares
text_by_object_id.g3ea5e0fb254_4_361: One app. One water layer. Clear roles.
text_by_object_id.g3ea5e0fb254_4_362:
▸  inDrive — demand, trip discovery, booking, payment and customer care.

▸  Navier — electric hydrofoil fleet, charging, fleet software and operating playbook.

▸  Local operator — licensed crews, terminals and day-to-day service.

▸  Authorities — route permission, waterfront access and oversight.
text_by_object_id.g3ea5e0fb254_4_447:
1.  Name an inDrive executive sponsor and Egypt market lead.
2.  Select one Hurghada or Sharm route for joint diligence.
3.  Source route demand, fares, terminal access and an operating partner before a launch decision.
text_by_object_id.g3ea5e0fb254_4_331: Choose one Red Sea route, prove the local operating case, and connect it to the complete journey.
text_by_object_id.g3eec5122801_0_692: What is and is not in the Egypt proposal
text_by_object_id.g3eec5122801_0_693: Five Red Sea routes are shown. Cairo is distribution context only. Financial totals wait for route-level demand and fares.
text_by_object_id.g3eec5122801_0_696:
▸  Hurghada → Three routes
      Giftun Island, Sahl Hasheesh and Soma Bay

▸  Sharm El Sheikh → Two routes
      Ras Mohammed and Sharks Bay

▸  Cairo → Distribution context
      no marine route proposed

▸  Financial case → Five routes
      advance after demand and fare evidence
